I love cinnamon or coconut on just about anything but I was highly disappointed with this treat. Good thing it was not what I came for. I would not order it again. Now about that walnut chocolate chip cookie... OMG! What a gooey, chewy, chocolate chip goodie!! To be honest, I can not and did not, finish this treat in one sitting. I cut 1/4 piece, wrapped it in foil, and lightly warmed it in the oven. Best way to have it! It was so soft and went perfect with my evening tea. The $4 price tag is not that bad either. Especially considering the size. I enjoyed that cookie for several days.
The cookies are to die for. I had the chocolate chip ball cookie when some coffee and was totally blissed out for like an hour

We're thrilled to hear that our chocolate chip walnut cookie paired with coffee brought you so much joy. Thanks for sharing your experience and for the awesome rating. Hope to see you again soon for another round of cookie bliss! Warmly, The Levain Team

The best cookie I have ever had in my life. I'm always here whether it be for a snack, post-exam treat, or picking cookies up as gifts for friends or to travel with. I recently brought a dozen with me to Atlanta for a Thanksgiving dinner and they were an absolute hit! All 4 flavors are amazing but my favorites are the chocolate peanut butter and the oatmeal raisin. These are normally cookies I would not prefer but Levain Bakery has completely changed my opinion of them. Can't get enough of these massively delicious cookies that have the best flavors and textures a cookie could possibly have!
I had the chocolate walnut cookie which is the most popular item. It was nice and crunchy on the outside and gooey on the inside. A little treasure-a must stop!

Super quick service from this location! I had never been before so had to check out the hype with Levain bakery! I went on a Saturday morning around 10:30 AM and there was no line so I didn't have to deal with the crazy lines every one's always talking about. I got the two chip chocolate cookie and my mom got the famous walnut one. I found that the two chip one was extremelyyy sweet (even for someone who absolutely loves chocolate and sweets). I didn't try the walnut one because I'm allergic to it but both my mom and brother said they couldn't even taste the walnuts and agreed it was too sweet. As the price point, I thought $5 was completely reasonable since the cookie was HUGE. Overall, if you like Levain Bakery, it's probably best to go in the mornings since it seems to be there are less lines but not sure if I would personally be going back!

I first discovered Levain Bakery because they won NYC's Munch Madness 2016 for their walnut chocolate chip cookie. I am so glad I did! Their cookies if we can call them that are in a league of their own. Instead of being flat, they are tall, round, and incredible moist. Beware, each cookie packs in about 600-700 calories. I once made the mistake if giving a whole cookie to each of my children. I knew the cookies were over the top when my children couldn't even finish the cookie and said they were full. That has never happened before. Since 2016, my favorite cookie has become their oatmeal raisin -- cranberry raisin? -- cookie. Its crumbly and moist texture makes it a cross between a scone and a cookie and is the best oatmeal cookie I've ever had. My kids have gravitated more towards the double chocolate cookie as well. Of late, the walnut chocolate chip cookies have been sightly undercooked, with a gooey center of undercooked cookie dough. I told the bakery and they said I should just wait to eat it because it is like that when it is fresh out of the oven. So, basically, they didn't believe me! I ate it 1 hour, 6 hours and 12 hours after purchasing and it was still undercooked in the center. I will still eat this heavenly dessert, but it makes me think twice before buying it as a gift for someone.
I really enjoy the cookies and the cake my only issue is the cake slices are VERY SMALL. And there's no incentive when you buy any cookies like any coupon.
Hi Beverley, thanks for sharing your thoughts with us. We're thrilled to hear you enjoy our cookies and cake. We appreciate your feedback and hope to have you back soon! Warmly, The Levain Team

You can avoid the lines by trying this location of the bakery chain. I got a dark chocolate peanut butter chip cookie: to me, I still think they bake their cookies too little. Most of the cookie I got was uncooked inside, and made me nauseous. It tasted good, but it's not what I look for in a cookie, which must be baked all through. No reason to go back.

While celebrating my Bestie's birthday an impromptu trip to Levain took place as we waited for another party member. Small shop with great service and a bunch of goodies to choose from.  With a cookie explosion seemingly taking place in the city Levain is a long time contender and a good competitor. However they are not a one trick pony. They do Cookies, Cakes, Muffins, Coffee and etc. I honestly couldn't remember if and when I had Levain's previously and with an unofficial Cookie Challenge presented to me by fellow yelper Alana D. I was intrigued to try a cookie as I purchased my bestie a very large slice of lemon pound cake. The chocolate chip walnut cookie was oversized full of chips and a good amount of walnuts that didn't overpower the cookie. Sweet and gooey and nice weather warm or not. Overall a good treat... let's face it, its hard to go wrong with sugar, chocolate and carbs. Lol Just A Note: As the cookies are big, the suggested cookie care instructions are recommended.
Just get extra for later, you're going to want more. The cookies are perfection. Indulge yourself because it's worth it.
Thanks for the sweet words. We're thrilled to hear you enjoyed our cookies. Hope to see you again soon for another round of cookie perfection! Warmly, The Levain Team

It is a sin to have cookies this good. Like I don't even eat cookies like that, sugar is evil as far as I am concern, but evil is this heavenly, then I have been sadly mistaken for most of my life. Take me back to New York, I need another monster chocolate cookie so I can live again. That just about sums it up!

I discovered Levain Bakery many years ago while living in NYC. It has been 16 years since I moved away, and they are STILL one of the few places I go out of my way to visit whenever I return to NYC. My favorites are their brioche, especially the chocolate chip version, and any of the cookies. Give them a try! You won't be sorry. P.S. Don't be deterred by a line. The wait is worth it!
Got the vegan cookie. Kinda expensive for a cookie, but it was a decent size. I'm glad I tried it, but I probably wouldn't go again. Definitely worth at least a visit.

Thank you for giving our Vegan & GF Chocolate Chip Walnut cookie a try. We hope you'll reconsider and give us another chance to impress you with our delicious treats. Your support means a lot to us! -The Levain Team

Five dollars for a chocolate chip cookie is highway robbery. But I'll easily be robbed because those cookies were delicious. Next time I'll just come with cash because I think they do a surcharge if you pay with a card. The place is pretty busy and there was a line out the door, which kind of shows that It's a good place to eat at.

Not to be dramatic but I'd do anything for these cookies. They are a buttery and chocolatey amazing gift to earth with a nice crisp outside but super gooey and moist inside. I have a huge sweet tooth so I'm bias, but I seriously love these cookies and go every time I'm in New York. If you aren't a huge fan of sweets, I'd recommend getting some milk for the side to wash everything down with. YUM.
Banana chocolate.chip slice was tasty, moist and flavorful! Iced coffee was great! Will return!
The cookies are good.  The service was quick and they were pleasant.  I ordered on line snd picked it up.  I would go back again.

Thank you for your kind words, Chrissy. We're delighted to hear you enjoyed our cookies and had a pleasant experience with our team. We can't wait to welcome you back for more delicious treats!  -The Levain Team

Not that Levain needs my review, but I will quickly say they deserve all five of these stars. Warm and slightly gooey on the inside every time. I always get the chocolate chip with walnut, but you can't go wrong with any of them. Always a stop I make if I'm nearby one of their locations.

It's a GIFT and a CURSE that I discovered that Levain Bakery was literally just around the corner from my Air BnB in Harlem on the LAST DAY that I was staying there. I bought one of each cookie (which was a small fortune) and brought them to my friends house as a hostess gift. We ended up opening a bottle of champagne and tasting each cookie. Chocolate chip walnut was my favorite. No wait, oatmeal raisin. The chocolate chip peanut butter was too rich. No, I take it back, just eat a small bite of it to feel completely satisfied. UNBELIEVABLE.

The staff is really nice and friendly. She indulged in my excitement to finally try Levain's. The cookies are better when warm. However, my only gripe with this place is that everything is $5 each. In my opinion, I don't think it's worth $5 for a cookie, but to each their own. It's still a must-try for foodies alike.

Calling them a cookie is an understatement. It's a hefty pastry with a gooey moist interior. Think of a cross between a cake and cookie. It's 4 dollars for a cookie which astonishes me but it's literally a meal. You only need one!! My cookie was straight out the oven. So here is the trick. Give it an hour or so to firm up. The anticipation will kill you but it's worth it. The exterior gets nice and crunchy while the inside is still pleasantly soft.

Levain is the best! They have a new cookie now with coconut. I like the classic but no coconut for me. The peanut butter chocolate is the best. The two chip chocolate chip is 2nd best but not by much. Love this spot and every location is consistent! 5 stars.
This place is dangerous for your diet. The Walnut Chocolate Chip cookies are a must have.
We're so glad you enjoyed! -The Levain Team :)

My first bite of their famous chocolate cookie was a bit unimpressive. I got here 20 minutes after the opened, and there was no line. I got my cookie right away, but it was cold. Surprisingly, however, the chocolate chips inside were still gooey. What kind of sorcery is this?! Its a good cookie, but I don't think I would go out of my way for it.
Very good caramel coconut chocolate chip cookie! Texture was perfect, gooey inside, soft with light crunch texture outside. I would recommend! Service was very nice. Thank you!

A friend treated me to some desert here, we got some chocolate chip cookies and I had to try the Lemon cake (my favorite), unfortunately the lemon cake was too bitter for my taste but I fell in love with the chocolate chip cookies, so warm & Delish! Small little bake shop with very friendly workers. I'll be back for more cookies!

You know you are one special person if l bring you a Levain cookie or a slice of their amazing lemon, banana nut and walnut slices of cakes.....OMG!! The #1 reason l patronize this bakery frequently is also due to their excellent customer service. Like the one l had this Sunday 2/25/2024 at their Harlem location with the manager Destiny. Destiny was super courteous in making my very complicated order for 15 cookies and cakes were arranged correctly. She took her time in placing the cookies and cakes delicately in the boxes beautifully....appreciate it Destiny Also, she is also quite pretty!!!!
A very popular brunch spot in Los Angeles is Republique. I have been here a few times and have to say they are always busy with tourists, workers, and overall just wanting some good food.
Cozy little corner coffee shop walking distance to Hollywood blvd it's a very clean and cute little pit stop before starting my day.

One of the best brunches I ever had in LA! It's a wait until you get seated but the line moves pretty fast. We went around 12:30 and got a place to sit at 1:15 The restaurant closes at 2 pm for their brunch menu We ordered two omelettes one blue berry pan cake and one Turkish eggs. Everything was delicious right from coffee to croissant! Make sure you have time in hand before you go to this place :) absolutely amazing!!

Food is very decent, I would give a 4.5, I like their baked goods more. Their egg Benedict is ok, not bad for sure. Thick cut bacon is salty, and toast is very fresh. Ambiance is where it shines, very cool looking interior. Service is fine, they get what you ask for. Just beware parking is very hard, and wait time is long so plan ahead. Definitely a go to spot if you visit LA.

5 stars for food, especially the strawberry passion fruit pie and baguette, we love it The place is noisy and crowded if you like quiet time to eat and chat with friends, here is not a good choice. The price is high and they charged team benefits 4%.... We will come back for these delicious food.

While visiting Los Angeles, I had heard about this popular restaurant located in the mid-Wilshire area serving a variety of French inspired dishes and garnering high praises from visitors. I ordered the escargot, dover sole, salmon, prawns, fries and risotto.  Although, some dishes were good the majority were disappointing and totally missed the mark. The Salmon was lukewarm and was sent back. The Prawns were without question the biggest disappointment. By far these were the smallest prawns I've ever had anywhere and for the price one would've truly expected more. Overall, the meal was good but not great. The service was poor and lacked structure, creating a chaotic and rushed atmosphere. Throughout my entire dining experience and other than the times of me personally calling over my server, he was inattentive, lacked personality and never made me feel welcomed. Although, it appeared the staff worked as a team it never seemed cohesive and what one might expect from an establishment of this caliber. The restaurant was crowded but I did see several staffers seemingly with little to do, which is why the lack of table service surprised me. Kudos, to the manager who did walk over and apologized for the salmon and provided me with a $50.00 gift card towards a future visit. This was very thoughtful and appreciated.

A good friend and I went out for a celebratory dinner at Republique on Tuesday. Food was amazing, ambiance was great and service was very good! Great vibe all around so let's get into it. Ambiance: From what I understand the building dates back to 1928 and was commissioned by Charlie Chaplin as an office space. ...some office! It's kind of a mixture of French. Gothic meets Spanish colonial with high ceilings, dramatic archways, and really makes for an interesting restaurant atmosphere. One can tell that this was built during the Los Angeles boom. Where real money was spent on the electrical and romantic structures. I kind of felt like I was in a monastery or private Hacienda - very unique and very Los Angeles. Food: overall 5 stars. We decided to cleanse our pallet with a glass of Rene Geoffroy 1er cru, Expression champagne: 5 stars Velvety, fine bubbles. Very good depth to this wine - starts out a little crisp and mineral on the tongue, then turns into a brioche and kind of a dry chalky finish on the palate. My first time trying this champagne and I found it to be delicious and sophisticated; perfect accoutrement to our oysters. We were given an amuse bouche (see photo) and it was the most perfect bite. I don't even know how to begin to describe it so I'll just refrain. East and West Coast Oysters: 5 stars Fishers island and kumamoto with barrel-aged mignonette. Delicious and perfectly shucked. The kumamoto were a little creamy, but not too much and the fisher islands were perfectly briny, good firmness to them.  The mignonette had a bit of cracked peppercorns in it and that was quite interesting in a great way. My friend and I decided that we could both make a meal out of these oysters alone. Baguette: 5 stars wow. The best baguette this side of the Atlantic ocean.  Served with Rodolphe Le Meunier butter, this was a real treat. This baguette and butter will set you back $15 but it is worth every cent. I highly encourage everyone to order this and the waiters and other patrons will tell you the same. I'm so glad we did this. Japanese Hamachi Crudo: 5 stars Tender Hamachi served with a strawberry Thai basil nuoc cham... very unique and delicious dish. I would order again. I'm typically not the kind of person to mix sweet berries with savory food, but this was the perfect balance of texture flavors, sweet and heat. Caramelized Walla Walla Sweet onion tart: 5 stars This is a very interesting tart served with chunks of Applewood, smoked bacon and aged Gruyere. This eats more like a very thin crust pizza wonderful texture, crispy thin crust with sweet onion, jam, melted Greer cheese, and crispy yet chewy chunks of applewood smoked bacon. Great flavors great texture (see photo). Frederic Esmonin 2023 Pinot Noir: 5 stars I remember notes of black cherry red currants, more of an earthy and heavier wine compared to the lighter pinot noirs I've had before. Napa Valley Lamb Rack: 4 stars (5 star lamb, 3 star polenta). Mixed feelings about this one. Lamb was cooked perfectly.  Great on-the-bone flavor and I could have licked the lamb jus off my plate. The dish also had roasted baby artichokes which were good, but the issue we had was the polenta.  I've had polenta before, and I don't remember it being so sweet. The polenta does come with mushroom and merguez sausage to help bring some depth and savoriness to the dish but it needed more help.  We did not finish this side, and we were disappointed but it's not the end of the world. Opera Cake: 5 stars There are times where I wish I can make something so delicious that people will talk about it for days after they eat it. The opera cake is a solid 5 stars I dessert choice.  My friend and I are not big chocolate people, but our waiter highly encouraged us to give this a try, and since we were having a celebratory dinner, we decided that a cake was in order. The texture on this cake was amazing. Smooth ganache with light sponge cake, crispy layer of roasted hazelnut. Just the right amount of richness and decadence. I'm glad we went out of our comfort zone and ordered the opera cake.  I highly recommend this dessert. Service: 5 stars. Jared was a waiter and he was attentive, possessed a good knowledge of the menu items and was able to offer helpful insight on the menu items. There is a whole team working to buss dishes, replace silverware and ensure water glasses are always topped off. I should also mention a man by the name of (I think) Quang; appeared to be either manager or a type of lead staff member. Very attentive and has a very keen eye to detail. I thank him for bringing me my second glass of wine when my first ran empty, and ensuring that my friend and I had everything we needed throughout the night. I look forward to coming back to Republique.

Hey, let me get this out of the way: Valet parking- $14, employees personnel fee: 4% onto your bill. The tip starts at 20-% at the register unless you change it. I felt like I was handing out money  for everything other than the food... Wifey had Quiche and a Rosè. She didn't like it, but ate it anyway. I had the Burger, which came with crispy fries that were really tasty!the Burger was cooked well and was amazingly good. The service was great and the environment was very busy and the movement was fast. Would I return? Sure, but just make sure you have at least $100. ‍

Came here around 11 am on a Saturday and there was a line. We waited about 15-20 minutes to get to the cashier to order. You order first and then find a table to sit at. We ordered the Filipino adobo fried rice, potato pancake, mango calamansi pie, a creme brulee pastry and another blueberry croissant pastry. Everything was delicious! Our favorite was the potato pancake, which came with pieces of salmon lox and eggs on top. The potato pancake was crispy and had a pancake texture and it was so interesting. The flavors all blended well together. Would highly recommend ordering! The Filipino adobo fried rice was also delicious and very flavorful. It had a kick to it even without adding the sriracha! Out of all the pastries, our favorite was the mango calamansi pie. They had just brought out a new whole pie as we were ordering so we had to order a slice. It wasn't too sweet and the cream wasn't too heavy either. Would definitely order again! The other pastries were also not too sweet and were tasty. Service was excellent! We received our food fairly quickly considering how packed it was. The restaurant has a lot of seating but République is pretty popular so it gets packed. There is street meter parking out in front. Would recommend!

Umm... can I live here?? We stopped by for brunch and left completely impressed. First things first ,the ambiance is stellar: airy, bright, and absolutely beautiful. I was smitten at first glance. And then came the bakery display, which honestly took my breath away. Once I managed to tear myself away from the space itself, I was blown away by the variety and the intricate detailing--things I'd only ever seen on shows like The Great British Bake Off. We ordered brunch along with a few pastries and beverages, and since it was Thanksgiving weekend, we also took home a pecan pie. It turned out to be a huge hit with our friends and was gone in a single sitting. Pricing is definitely on the higher side, but the quality and overall experience make it worthwhile. Highly recommended.

We had a very lovely evening. The restaurant is stunning. The Hostess was very kind, warm greeting and enjoyable to chat with while we waited for our table. Our waiter was excellent. The drinks were good. Our favorite thing was the baguette, which was incredible. And the taster of potato leek soup that came out with it. That pairing alone we could've eaten for dinner. It was followed by the beef fat fries and the half roast chicken. The mains were very good, but again could have had that baguette and soup for dinner! The one Complaint I have as is the prices are pretty high and when you balance the experience with the cost, I'd probably give it four stars. $72 for a quality 1/2 roast chicken. When the cost goes up that much, your expectation goes up with it.

Very much enjoyed our dinner here.  Ambiance is lovely, noise level and therefore energy high, fun music loudly playing, lots of lovely people all around, beautiful sights to look at as most food stations are displayed for your enjoyment, and great food & drink. We started with the pan dripping and bread, which was very good but we all agreed the bread was phenomenal with just plain cold butter.  We moved on to the sushi grade mackerel on toast, which was delicate and amazing (my friend cut her mouth on the toast bc it was too darkly toasted).  We then had the charcuterie plate, which was lovely especially the duck pâté (buttery and delicious) and pork confit. Our main entrees were the pork chop and belly, which was prepared nicely.  It didn't blow me away but it was tasty.  We also had the 14 oz rib eye, which I enjoyed but not every one at the table did.  We all agreed the temp at which it was cooked was not near high enough.  The best steaks are high temp to sear the meat and marbling, and nice and juicy pink in the middle, as far as our table was concerned. We had two desserts. The hazelnut donut and ice cream was just okay, and the chocolate cake with sesame foam and black sesame ice cream was a lovely presentation and delicious. I didn't give 5 stars bc timing was poor on courses and the very high quality meat entrees were not done as well as expected especially for the $$$.  Still had a lovely time and am happy to go again soon.

A very popular brunch spot in Los Angeles is Republique. I have been here a few times and have to say they are always busy with tourists, workers, and overall just wanting some good food. You have to order first and then get a number to put down on your table. The avocado toast is delicious!!! If you love avocados this one is gigantic and I literally couldn't finish it. For dessert, we also ordered a cheesecake and had a taste of this creamy delicious cheesecake. It is one of the best! They have long tables or small chairs and tables as well. So you can come with a large group or even a small one just enjoy the inside of this spot. It is quite pretty.

Long overdue, but this spot absolutely deserves a shoutout. We came here for Valentine's Day and ended up having one of those meals you keep talking about long after, it was that good. Every one of the six courses hit, and we couldn't resist ordering a few rounds of cocktails to keep the celebration going. Standouts for me were the kanpachi crudo and the cauliflower agnolotti (Maine lobster with winter black truffle), both beautifully plated and packed with flavor. You can tell a lot of thought went into each dish. Service was polished and accommodating, and the ambiance was beautiful, perfect for a special night out. The pacing felt a bit quick at times; a little more breathing room between courses (and cocktails) would've made the experience even better. Definitely book ahead, this place is always buzzing and has definitely earned its spot as one of LA's go-to dining destination.

this spot has been on my list of places to try for a while and i finally had to chance to try it! the line seemed pretty long but it went by really quickly, i think we waited around 15-20 minutes. you order first and then it's open seating. i ordered the: potato pancake kimchi fried rice caramel banana pudding bread with vanilla cream short rib burrito my favorite was the potato pancake, i loved how crispy the pancake part was and it paired so well with all the toppings, very creative and unique dish. i also really liked the banana pudding bread, it was crispy and soft and had a really great banana flavor which went well with the vanilla cream on top. the burrito and kimchi fried rice were just okay, the meat was rlly tender for the fried rice but the dish itself doesn't rlly taste like kimchi fried rice. overall loved the vibes and ambiance of the interior and i would come back for the potato pancake and to try other desserts

Good food but with a casual atmosphere. The space was a little tight and saw a few families with strollers struggling a bit. The line was out the door when I arrived but it went by fairly quickly, and staff were pretty efficient with clearing tables and what not. You order and pay with the cashier then hope you can snag a table! We were able to get one fairly quickly though :) They have solid coffees and pastries so I can see myself going back for that vs a full meal. The breakfast was delicious and all the toasts they brought out looked so appetizing. Food!! I shared the Pork Adobo Fried Rice which was delicious and the pork was so tender, and the blueberry pancake. If you're a pancake fan, get this! Its big, light, and fluffy. Im not  much of a pancake person so I think I would've preferred the waffle or a toast bc they come with more toppings. All the pastries we tried were delicious! Uber Brioche Blueberry Pop Tart Banana Dulce de Leche Salted Caramel brioche ( SO GOOD)

Alright so Republique had been on my Los Angeles dining bucket list for quite some time and I'm pleased to report I finally made it there this past Friday evening for dinner. It was my first visit and I'd say that overall, it met expectations. We had reservations right when dinner service began at 5:30pm which was great for me as I don't stay out too late, hehe. Despite that being the only reservation available, the restaurant did not actually fill up too quickly. Either way, arriving early allowed us to settle in nonetheless. Parking is pretty much valet only ($17) which I suppose is typical for this part of LA. So anyway, if you've never been to Republique before, the atmosphere alone is worth a visit. The dining room feels almost Harry Potter-esque/cathedral-like with its soaring glass ceiling and tall brick walls. It feels pretty special and unique. On this particular Friday evening, our strategy was simple: order a lot and share everything. The wait staff/menu encourages this approach and we were told that 5-7 dishes is a good number, which is about what we ordered. A few standouts from the meal included the Kumamoto oysters which were fantastic. They were incredibly fresh and I loved the mignonette sauce. The bread with pan drippings was deceptively delicious and quite unforgettable. I could have happily kept dipping bread into the savory goodness of the pan drippings all night. Even the butter was delicious! The agnolotti pasta was another highlight. Perfectly cooked without feeling heavy. For mains, I really enjoyed the striploin steak which was cooked beautifully and full of flavor. We also ordered the lamb rack which was just as impressive and plated beautifully if I do say so myself! The hamachi crudo was probably the only dish that I didn't love which is too bad because it was one I really wanted to try. It wasn't bad by any means but just a bit unexpected in flavor and not my personal favorite of the evening. Service was solid overall. Our server (Jared, according to the receipt) kept things moving smoothly, though he didn't introduce himself by name and the interactions felt a little odd, especially considering the restaurant of this caliber. And, one thing I didn't notice until reviewing the receipt later was the 4% service charge added for employee health and medical benefits. I completely support restaurants taking care of their staff, but I do wish this had been mentioned more clearly during the dining experience. It's noted on the receipt, but I'm not sure it was noted on the menu. A meal here  is definitely a splurge but sometimes you just have to treat yo'self. The food, the atmosphere, and the overall experience were five stars. Next time, I'd love to return for breakfast or brunch. For now, Republique delivered a memorable first visit and I'm already looking forward to next time!

Republique Review THE FOOD: Republique absolutely delivers where it matters most--the food. The standout was the kimchi pastry, which was both inventive and genuinely delicious, not just creative for the sake of it. The quiche was authentic & divine. The viral potato pancake absolutely lived up to the hype, satisfying, and worth ordering. The kimchi fried rice was solid but didn't quite hit the same level as the others; it could definitely benefit from more meat to round it out. On the other hand, my husband couldn't stop talking about the croque madame, which was clearly a hit. THE SERVICE: This is a pay-and-seat-yourself setup, so don't expect traditional table service. That said, the system runs smoothly and efficiently. It's more casual and self-directed, but it fits the overall experience and keeps things moving without feeling chaotic. THE VIBE: Republique has a lively, bustling energy that makes it feel like a true destination spot. It's busy, a bit loud, and very much part of the charm. The atmosphere leans more toward upscale casual than fine dining, perfect for a relaxed but still elevated meal.

Parking lot is tiny and valet parking is pretty much mandatory You walk in and get funneled into the line of ordering desserts while you browse through the daily fresh made breads and cakes. At the end of the line, there's two kiosks that will take your order. My wife and I went during lunch time so it's cafeteria style seating and you get a number sign after you order and the servers will bring your food to you. The basque cheesecake was the most memorable item here and most other items on the menu are ok/above par. The ambiance and the decor is what really draws people in. For dinner service, reservations are required!

We came here for my birthday and we loved it! This is a great restaurant with phenomenal service, and the interior of the restaurant is nicely designed! It gives it a real classy LA vibe. Food was amazing! We had the braised shortrib, lobster pasta, pork belly and caviar, and I forget the other dish.. Also had Berry tres leches for dessert! Highly recommended! Street parking!

It's not for no reason Republique was awarded with Michelin and prolly also first name LA peeps would call out when being asked top brunch place in town. I completely got the line in front almost always looked discouraging but this did worth the wait. Their brunch menu, their pastries and cakes line up, their gorgeous dining space; name it and they simply ticked all boxes. No single dish tried so far wasn't impressive. We're back to host our friend who's LA first timer last week and arrived there around an hour before lunch, when the line wasn't bad and moved speedily! Got their crowd's fave Maine Lobster omelette which might sound simple yet also simply outstanding with generous chunks of fresh lobster with lusciously creamy sauce. Having been a fan of their pastries since my week 1 moving into LA, I never skipped trying different ones when coming here. This time it's the seasonal Ube Coconut Almond Croissant, which I certainly fell for and still thought about. Pretty bold ube and coconut taste, but still let the almond being the star!

Visited this place on a recent Sunday morning. Parked in the lot adjacent to the establishment before the valet dudes even showed up. Got to the entrance about 25 minutes before opening hoping to avoid being in a long line, which I heard is pretty common here. Was pleased to see no one else waiting in line. By the time the place opened, there were only about a dozen or so people in line. Kind of regret showing up so early, but absolutely do not regret coming here. The selection of bakery goods here is pretty impressive. I could have ordered like two dozen things since everything looked so delectable, but I exercised restraint. Can't afford to gain too many more pounds. I ended up getting the cinnamon roll, traditional croissant, chocolate chip cookie, and bomboloni. At the register, I also ordered the short rib burrito and lemonade. I paid for my food right then and there, which I appreciated. That meant I could leave whenever I wanted once I was done eating. Anyway, after paying for the food, I was given a coffee cup with a number on it and informed that I could sit wherever I wanted. I could talk about how cool the interior looks, but you can browse through the interior photos and judge for yourself. I felt like I was in one of those themed restaurants at Disneyland. While I waited for the burrito at a table, I started trying out the baked goods I got. Man oh man. I loved everything I got here. The cookie was packed with chocolate goodness and had a wafer thin crispy crust that was amazing. The cinnamon roll, which had a crunchy and sugary exterior, was delicious. My favorite bakery item was the croissant. It was crunchy and flaky on the outside and soft and chewy on the inside. There's no way I can go back to eating store bought croissants after this. The short rib burrito was a home run as well. It was so tasty. Loved that it had a slight kick to it. I should point out here that this is not one of those burritos you can grab and eat with your hands. You have to eat it with a fork and knife. Like an enchiladas. What makes this burrito distinctive is that it's got an egg on top of it, not inside it. This review is running super long even by my standards so I'll wrap it up soon. I have to mention that I even enjoyed their "lemonade." I'm not sure why they call it a lemonade when it tastes like blueberries and mandarin oranges, but who cares. It's refreshing as hell. One last thing to share. Just because you park next door and there's no valet guy around doesn't mean you get to park there for free. It's $14 whether you park the car yourself or not. Not sure how people can rate this place less than five stars, but everyone has their own opinion, heh. In my opinion, this is one of the best places around to have breakfast and that's saying a lot since there are a lot of great breakfast joints in the Los Angeles area.

One of the best bakery and brunch spots in all of LA! My husband and I visited on a weekend afternoon. The line looked seemingly long, but actually moved by pretty quickly. We were able to order some brunch foods as well as pastries in less than 15 minutes. This is a casual restaurant during brunch hours, in which you order first and then seat yourself anywhere. It appears to be more formal during dinner hours. Bakery: The pastries here are absolutely wonderful. No wonder there is always a line out the door for them. The Creme Brulee Bomboloni has a soft, pillowy dough and a rich custard that is addicting to eat. Furthermore, I was super amazed by the Almond Dacquoise, which was light and airy. It had delicious layers of buttercream and a pleasant nutty flavor. There are many more standout pastries, some of which are seasonal. I wish I could try them all! Brunch: We ordered 2 things from the brunch menu. First, the BLT Benedict is a creative twist on traditional eggs Benedict. I really enjoyed this version with bacon, lettuce, and tomato. The eggs were poached perfectly, while the hollandaise sauce was mouthwatering good. As for the Maine Lobster and Dungeness Crab Omelette, it was the best omelette I've ever tasted. Both the lobster and crab complemented the eggs and cheese wonderfully. Highly recommend both these brunch items!

Tried Republique for the first time! Two of us had: arugula rigatoni $44 bucatini cacio e pepe $38 sparkling water $8 rodolphe le meunier butter $15 4 Kumamato $5 ea $20 2 cheeses $20 little gem salad $28 regalist pennsylvania golden chicken $72 remi jobard btl white wine $140 cuyama orchards apple tart $18 health LA 4% $16.04 Knocking off a huge star for the pasta. Big miss. Pasta was overcooked for both and a bit on mushier side. I did let staff know at the tail end of the meal for feedback. Bread was good! Wasn't charged for another one (but maybe it is included?) though the second one was on the burnt side. The chicken though! So good! Haven't had chicken like that in a long time. Everything else on the menu was good. Obviously on the pricier side meal, so hopefully the pasta is just a one-off. Server Bessie was great! We ended up parking on the street a few blocks down.

Came here for dinner with my mom and sister and it was a cute restaurant. The food was great we shared the short rib, lobster pasta, and tuna tartare which was good for 3 people! The vibe of the restaurant was really cute too. The waitress was also so kind and also from houston so we bonded about that! I definitely wanna come back and try more of the stuff on the menu bc everything sounds great + everything we got was delish
Came here for dinner and it was a cute restaurant. The food was great we shared the short rib, lobster pasta, and tuna tartare which was good for 3 people!

Ube Brioche (8.5/10): the brioche was super caramelized on top and the ube was a nice addition. Very impressive pastry! Black Sesame Mochi (6/10): nothing too impressive here. Tastes pretty average Baguette (5/10): not memorable. Bread was pretty average. Kimchi Fried Rice (6.5/10): not as good as the adobo, actually. Less flavor in the rice and it felt lacking somehow. Short rib was decent. Adobo Fried Rice (7.5/10): actually delicious! I was surprised to see a French restaurant serving Filipino food. The chicken was very tender and savory Brioche French Toast (7/10): pretty good. Nothing mindblowing. Breakfast Sandwich (8.5/10): actually surprisingly good. Looks very simple, but super flavorful. Loved the sausage. The interior of this place is very cool! Feels like you're dining in a mansion.

I just moved to the area and was thrilled when I saw République was walking distance to me. République is busy more times then not. And for good reason. It's recognized by the Michelin Guide and you'll see why when you visit. It's a beautiful open sunlight restaurant that has a big dining room filled with seating. I've only been in the breakfast/lunch service and you will wait in line to place your order. There are a bunch of delicious pastry options to choose from while in line. After you order, it's opening seating so you can sit wherever that's open. I've order the Koshihikari rice and the quiche from the pastry case. The rice is great, my boyfriend loved it! It's very flavorful and satisfying. The quiche is delicious and they rewarm it perfectly, the crust is perfect and flaky. I've gotten both the Vietnamese latte and the café con horchata. They are both okay, nothing out of this world. However, they do have other drinks that I do want to try. Like I said, they have a wonderful pastry case with plentiful of options. I've only tried the dulce de leche pound cake and it was fantastic! It's definitely a new favorite spot that I will be coming back on repeat. So much more to try!

Came here for a date night with my husband, and was completely blown away! I am so happy we finally were able to dine here. The ambiance, service, and quality of food were all 10/10! We ordered the blue fin tuna tartlet (packed with flavor in a tiny handheld tart!), baguette and butter (the world's SOFTEST bread!), yellowtail tartare (the zest!!! was def my fav), duck (so tender!) and the Campanelle pasta. We also got a side of fries that was so savory! To finish, we got the strawberry tiramisu, which was to die for. The service was quick, friendly and so thorough. We left feeling so full, and so excited to come back again! Would love to try the brunch sometime. Tip: valet parking for dinner hours is a standard rate of $17.

Yes, I know it's a fancy place. Yes, I know a lot of people go there just to take Instagram pictures but the food is legitimately good I mean really good. The interior is also classic French cafe and feels like they used french street views inside of the building. Friendly, well spoken staff, they clearly knew their food. Its an open kitchen and you can see the big grill. Yes, it's expensive but it's not overpriced. This is a great place to treat yourself or your loved ones..! can't believe I'm saying this, but the duck was better than the beef steak. The french fries were crispy pieces of perfection. The croquette was a crunchy morsel of bacony fat and potato. The tuna and caviar was my least favorite skip it... But then again, l've never been blown away by caviar.

My friend says this is one of her fave foodie spots. So let's see if they're pretty good eh or ew. They were on the Michelin guide and have a bunch of yummy looking pastries. I ended up getting their quiche slice and banana croissant thingy to try. The quiche had a buttery flakey crust with super creamy rich savory eggs and a good amount of spinach. My friend said it's the best she's ever had and she wasn't wrong. The croissant was nice and crispy flakey caramelized and buttery and had a soft gooey sweet yummy bananay middle. This place is kinda pricey but tastes good so it's lowkey pretty good. Quiche $8 Banana danish $5 Paid: $14.85

This has been on my list for quite some time, and I'm so glad we were able to check it off. Even on a Wednesday morning, it was so busy - I can only imagine how packed it gets on the weekend. We ordered the following: Iced latte (standard, nothing amazing) Cheesecake (so moist and delicious) Banana cream pie (husband preferred this - it was good, but the crust was a little tough) Short rib burrito (super flavorful) Potato pancake (we both loved this one - such a creative and beautiful dish) Lobster omelette (husband's favorite, but I prefer a Benedict) Steak frites (solid, cooked perfectly) We were able to snag street parking, but again, it was a weekday. Would love to come here again (but never over the weekend).

Came for breakfast on Saturday ~9:45am. Or is it brunch? - important to note the "lunch" portion of the menu doesn't go into effect until 11am. Line was a little bit out the door, but moved quickly enough. Busy and hectic right at the front as always -- pressure to choose your pastry items quickly before you order the menu items (food and drink) at the register. Do make sure you get a look at everything before choosing in the case there is something at the end you might want! After ordering and paying (FYI there is a service fee for staff members), you take your number to seating of your choice. Currently the outdoor patio area is closed for renovation (or remodeling or re...), so it's indoors only. We were a bigger group (6) so squeezed on the end of a shared table with two others and moved to have the whole table once they left mid-way through our meal. Food: * Brioche trench toast: An amazing thick piece of brioche that is light and sweet and toasted evenly. It barely needs the maple syrup, but of course we're adding it. * Chicken and biscuits: Not as gravy-forward as I would have liked, but great presentation, well cooked, etc. Had a little bit of spice but would have liked more! * Chocolate salted caramel cake: This may be my favorite chocolate cake in LA. I love chocolate cake and this is amazing (and the reason for the whole visit!). Breakfast starts off great with a slice of this. * Cinnamon bun: Not like the oozy sticky buns you may be thinking of but a pastry with cinnamon (-sugar?) on top and around. Was light, delicate and delicious. * Matcha-something (different than what's on the current published menu and I can't remember!): Ordered it hot and loved it. Parking is a bit tough - but can be found on the block parallel for 2 hours free on the weekend. Is this a surprisingly expensive brunch, yes, but a special place for a brunch outing with friends or visitors from out of town.

We finally were able to try Republique! Arrived around 10am on a Saturday and waited about 20 mins to order. When we left at 11am, the line was triple the length (come early!). Pastries 10/10: WOW, they can't go wrong. We tried multiple and we couldn't get enough What we ordered from best to worse: 1.Breakfast quesadilla: basically the French version of a Oaxacan tlayuda. The cauliflower was such a tasty twist to what could have been a basic dish. It was loaded with flavor and was a very good size. We ended up sharing it! 2.Mediterranean eggs: probably the most unique egg dish I've tried. Taste was 10/10, but the portion was very small. It was two eggs in a puddle of yogurt which tasted amazing but left us wanting more. 3.BLT Benedict: the least memorable from what we ordered. Still had fresh ingredients and tasted lovely but was pretty basic. Wouldn't order again. As expected, the ambiance was amazing and made us want to hangout and just enjoy the space. Such a beautiful building with lots of LA history.

Came once for breakfast/brunch and once for dinner- can say both experiences were splendid! Though, I may be a bit partial to the breakfast/brunch here bc I love pastries and theirs are spectacular (especially the canele!). Highly recommend to treat yourself to a dinner here, even the bread and butter were very memorable. We ordered 1-2 dishes from each section of their menus and not a single one was a let down. If you get the chicken (dinner menu), disclaimer it is not a big bird/portion is smaller than you'd expect. However, the service and flavor pairings of everything made up for it. No complaints from me(or my family)! Can't wait to be back.

This place is very popular so expect a line and a bit of a wait. But the line goes reasonably fast and despite the number of people you can generally find a seat. The skylights make for a very pleasant morning dining experience with wonderful natural light without three wind or weather. I ordered the Croque Madame wondering, how good can a ham and cheese sandwich be? The answer is, pretty damn good! The gruyere cheese is fantastic, the chopped ham was the perfect amount and the fried egg on top was just decadent! More places have to copy this! My wife had the lobster omelette and it was also very good. The flavor was mild but very nice. The Belgian waffle was fine ... But not as special. Warning: the valet parking is $14, which is pretty steep if you consider that you're probably only going to be here an hour or so. The one thing I would change is the choice of drinks. If you don't want coffee you can have ginger ale or lemonade. That's it. Would it really kill you to offer some diet Coke? I had the ginger ale and it was just too much. I had to water it down to make it drinkable. I was considering dropping down to 4 stars for the drinks and parking ... But this is about food so I kept it at 5.

I love this place for brunch and dinner.  Great ambience and solid abc creating dishes.  I do wish they tools reservations for brunch since ur the only obstacle from me going more often.  The lines and time are too much and so I don't go as often.  I'd rather get some pastries to go.

Finally getting around to posting this.. definitely a latepost, but this meal was too good not to share. Ambiance: The architecture here is just unmatched. Walking into that historic building with the massive glass ceilings and all that natural light felt like a total "healing moment." It's always buzzing and full of life, but it still feels airy and sophisticated. Truly one of the most beautiful dining spaces in LA. Food: Everything we ordered was a 10/10. The French Toast is legendary for a reason.. thick, perfectly caramelized on the outside, and just melts in your mouth. You can really tell they use top-tier ingredients. Even the savory dishes were so fresh and well-balanced. It's the kind of food that makes you want to come back the next day. Service: Despite how busy the place was, the staff handled everything like total pros. Professional, attentive, and they kept the vibe smooth throughout the meal. Overall: Look, between the valet, the menu prices, and tips, the bill definitely adds up.. but honestly? For an experience this high-quality, I don't mind the cost at all. It is worth every penny for the vibe and the flavor. Can't wait to head back!

Went to République on La Brea and Wilshire and really liked it. The place is beautiful and has a great vibe, but it does get pretty busy. The pastries were amazing...definitely the highlight. Food overall was good, though a bit pricey for what you get. I'd come back, especially for the pastries.

My sister and I took our cousin out for a late birthday brunch. The line was really long but went by pretty fast. Whether you're want to purchase some pastries or order some food, you'll need to fall in line regardless. While we were in line, of course we ordered some pastries: seasonal bread pudding, berry tres leches cake, creme brûlée bomboloni, pandan cookie, and spinach tomato quiche with caramelized onions & cheese. As for brunch, we ordered a brioche french toast, lobster omelette, Filipino adobo fried rice, and chicken & biscuit. For drinks we ordered a carafe mimosa and iced ube coconut matcha latte. While we looked for an open table to sit down. My cousin noticed one of our water drinking glasses was damaged so we flagged a server/busser. They mentioned it was the way the glasses were stacked and he proceeded to put his finger in the glass to show us the glass did not have any shards. Furthermore, he never gave us a new glass and was very rude. We had to flag another busser to get a new cup. Regardless of the mishap we encountered with the glasses, the food was extremely amazing! Each entree we ordered had their own unique flavor and taste. Would definitely come back although I hope not to encounter the same problem with glassware.

Had an end of year date a couple of weeks ago. The ambiance was beautiful, even though we waited a little bit to be seated for our reservation. Andrew D. was our server, and he went over the menu and concept, along with giving some recommendations. To drink, my fiancé had the Skyduster IPA and I had their passion fruit cocktail. Both were delicious. We ordered escargot en croute as an hors d'oeuvres, kurobata pork belly as a second course, then I ordered the venison with peppercorn jus and my fiancé had the halibut. A complimentary cup of mushroom soup was also served. We also got a baguette with the butter, and I selfishly ordered more bread so we could take it home with the butter. All of it was delicious and unique, but they all felt familiar in the best way. The mushroom soup was a stunner, and my fiancé (who usually resents mushrooms) really enjoyed it. Our favorite dish was the pork belly; it was interesting because usually we eat crispy pork belly, but the textures and flavors of the dish were decadent but light. We would definitely come back for another special event. We had an amazing time and this meal will stick with us for a long time.

Great food! Folks taking orders were so kind and helpful. I ordered the lobster omelette and do not regret it. It was delicious! It came with a side salad that was fresh and tasty. Unfortunately, I finished my salad before taking a picture of my plate. I like the seating area. It's naturally lit and very clean. Restroom was also clean. I'm looking forward to returning and trying more items on the menu but have to be mindful of the cost. Omelette $28 Smoothie $10 + tip/tax Valet parking $14 + tip Easily a $65 breakfast for two items.

The croque madame was exceptional: the sandwich had a perfectly crispy crust and was filled with plenty of Gruyère cheese and fresh, non-deli looking ham. The salad on the side was refreshing as well. I also got the coconut cake with yuzu cream I think: it was pretty good, had a slight lemon flavor and not super sweet and had a lot of fresh coconut. You order at the front cashier and then find your own seat, which I prefer to waiting for a seat and server. It makes it pretty casual overall too, but most people seem to be dressed more smart casual than anything. Very good, looking forward to coming back.

Must have brunch spot when you visit LA! No reservations, must stand in line, order first, and then find a table. Worth the wait. Ordered the brioche french toast (best french toast I've had), the french omelette, and the Shakshouka. Great ambiance, and super enjoyable vibe overall.
Good croissants but the other pastries are weird. The service is fast. And the ambiance is hectic but super cool inside.

My first visit to Republique was a disappointment. Our entrees were unremarkable, the drinks tasted basic, and service was downright disappointing. I doubt I'll be giving their breakfast another shot. The long line and difficult parking situation on top of our lackluster experience pretty much seals the deal. We ordered the Short Rib Burrito and Adobo Fried Rice. The short rib was tough and the fried rice didn't taste like adobo. For such a well reviewed and renowned restaurant, our entrees were not up to par. I'm not sure if our interactions with the staff were influenced by the fact that we came in the day after thanksgiving, but everyone seemed to hate their job. We were really excited to finally try Republique after all these years, but our visit left us disillusioned.

I've had this restaurant on my try list for a very long time and this recent weekend I was able to take my wife here as she also was heavily interested in this restaurant. First impressions from us is that the wait time can be a bit off. We expected to wait about 30 minutes to an hour on a busy weekend (lunch hour) but we waited only about 10-15 minutes to get seated. PARKING: No designated lot, recommended to park in nearby residential streets (free) and take a walk over to the restaurant. For first time diners, this is a order then sit down type restaurant. With an amazing display of pastries along the way before taking your order. There's a booth window outdoors with a different line outside for ordering pastries only. With plenty of diners around, we thought it would be difficult to find seats but it was easier than we thought with plenty of diners going in and out of the restaurant after their meals. Also pretty nice that there's plenty of seats in the restaurant along with counters seating as well. Our first time visit consist of two pastries orders: - Creme Brulee Bomboloni ($4.50) - WOW, this is literally a mouthful of creme brulee BOMB. The cream absolutely melts in your mouth and it's full of flavor from the shell and the cream. Not very pricy and definitely worth a try. - Almond Dacquoise ($7) - This is by far the best pastry I've ever had. While the looks can deceive you, the pastry is soft and similar to a souffle style dish. Love the flavoring blast as you taste the pastry. Very well presented and definitely a pastry that you could get addicted to. HIGHLY RECOMMEND Brunch items ordered: - MAINE LOBSTER AND DUNGENESS CRAB OMELETTE ($28) - Classic omelet dish, filled with gruyere cheese, spinach, hollandaise sauce, and a side of sauced salad. Presented super neatly, eggs were cooked perfectly and cut very easily. The salad complimented the omelet extremely well. Not very salty, would say that you can't really go wrong with this dish if you're having a hard time deciding what to order. Simple and delicious. - BLT BENEDICT ($25) - Similar to the omelet, this was super flavorful. Full of ingredients that include bacon, avocado, arugula, balabrian, sauce, and a poached egg. Loved everything about this benedict, very savory, and not very salty considering the ingredients. Highly recommend if you want a fast bite. Overall, a wonderful restaurant, amazing brunch spot. Love the interior as they have a open kitchen, and it's pretty interior with their medieval modern styling. Love how spacious it is even when it's packed. Amazing food and service. Only con is that they don't take reservations for their brunch but they do for their dinner times. Different menu than brunch so my wife and I will definitely be back in the future to try their different menus.

The reason for the 3 Stars... They force a Healthy LA Tax on your bill that is not required by law. I asked them to remove that Tax and they refused. This Tax is meant to help the restaurant pay for employee health care. Proving Health Care to their employees is their responsibility, not the paying customers responsibility. The fee is exorbitant, cheap, and tacky! They won't tell you this up front. You have to look closely at your check and there's a line item called 'Healthy LA.' It's truly outrageous! Great Food, amazing staff, and beautiful location! Breakfast was really good and different! Portions were small and pricey. The restaurant was clean and there was plenty of seating. The servers were very attentive and friendly.

I came here for a birthday brunch with my friend on a Thursday afternoon. Seating is first come, first served, but we found a spot within about 5 minutes. You order at the front and they bring the food out to you, which worked out smoothly. We shared the ricotta toast, and it was amazing. I never had anything like this before. It truly melts in your mouth.  I ordered the regular breakfast (minus the bacon, subbed for avocado), and my friend got the steak. The fries that accompanied the steak were the most crispiest flavorful fries I ever had. I felt bad I kept picking at my friends fries. We also picked up a scone and a cookie. Everything was absolutely delicious, incredibly fresh, and full of flavor. One thing I have to highlight is the French baguette with the butter and jam. OMG... SO mouthwatering. I would honestly come back just to buy a jar of their preserves. The pastries were wonderful, and my Vietnamese coffee was perfect. To top off the experience, I even saw a comedian there and got a selfie with him! The vibe was awesome, the food was fantastic, and the service was great. I'd love to come back for a weekend brunch. Highly recommend!

Food here is amazing and line for brunch or lunch moves quickly so don't be discouraged..  And it is worth the wait.    The coffees are delicious and we had the best egg custard deserts since we visit Portugal.    I had the kimchee rice with soft egg and beef which was filling and tasty and fantastic.  My partner had the egg sandwich with the most delicious bacon I have ever had.   The ingredients they use are incredible.   The staff friendly and helpful and we just loved everything about the experience!

We went in on a wet LA morning and were super happy with everything from the quick flow of the line to the table service, atmosphere, and quality and taste of the food. We took several pastries home to enjoy and it was all amazing. Definitely worth a return trip

Ahhh everything was incredible and I can see why there is usually a long line at Republique. We sampled several breakfast options on the menu and took home pastries to enjoy later and everything was a slam dunk. Service was quick, despite the line, and they were really efficient in taking everyone's orders and getting them out to the tables quickly without making patrons feel rushed.

I was shocked the line was so short, which was beautiful. We ordered the brioche french toast, avocado toast, and a french omelet. Loved the french toast. The french omelet had a waxy exterior, so it may have been sitting out for a min before being served. They have so many juices that look amazing and pastries to try.

So many choices!! And all the baked goods looked beautiful. Service was quite good. The atmosphere can't be beat with the warm LA weather and outdoor seating options. Breakfast bowl was tasty and so were the baked goods. Saw a celebrity there as well! Would definitely come back

Firstly, do not part at the lot, it's minuscule and $14 for brunch timing parking is steep. The lines were long but it moved quickly. You are quickly overwhelmed with the amount of pastry choices and very little time to decide. Once you picked out your pastries, you're able to order your entrées at the cashier and pay for your food. They give you a number and then off you go walking through the entire restaurant looking for a table. In our case, it was standing around waiting for someone to get up. The restaurant was full and yet they refused to open up the second floor for patrons. Our food arrived, and we still didn't have a table to sit in, which was frustrating. The five of us squeezed into a two top until a larger table was available. Once we were done with our meal, I noticed there were tables that were empty that were for dirty plates that were not cleared in time. The food was good but for the service and price for valet, would not recommend unless you were looking specifically to overpay for next to no service.

Other than the parking being a complete and utter shit show... the food and ambiance is 10/10. The must gets: Omelette Brioche French toast Kimchi fried rice Ricotta cheese toast (I believe the fruit on top is seasonal) the bread and cheese is amazing enough to get it! The fruit is a bonus. They have large space outside that is good for groups.

I'm sitting in the restaurant right now, leaving this review because I love this spot so much. I'm a regular here, so they give me free appetizers and desserts almost every time I come now. Whether you just want a cocktail, mocktail, app, dessert or full four course meal, this place is the bomb.  One of my favorite spots to go to in LA. Today I wasn't that hungry so just had a drink, appetizer and dessert and it blew my freaking mind.  Who knew you could make snow peas so extravagant? Worth every penny. Here's some pics from tonight and previous meals. Just realized I've been going here for over a year. Went by in a flash. I wish I could find the pic of the potato breakfast thing I had in the past here on my phone.  Also great sandwiches here.  Literally everything is delicious here.

Republique is the perfect brunch spot and I highly recommend. We ordered the short rib burrito, filipino adobo fried rice, baguette, and strawberry passion fruit cream pie. Everything was so delicious. Our favorite was the strawberry passion fruit cream pie. Wow!!! The taste was phenomenal and so tasty. The crust was perfectly cooked and I loved the strawberry and passion fruit cream. Everything melts in your mouth and we were both wanting more. We ate all of the dessert before our entree came to the table. The burrito and fried rice were both solid. I loved the baguette with the butter and jam. This restaurant has a very beautiful ambiance and it's perfect for date night or time with the girls. It's so cute for brunch. I've never been here for dinner so I kind of want to try and see how it is. We had the most perfect date experience here!!

Been to Republique for brunch and dinner and although I enjoyed both brunch is better.  The pastries and desserts here are quite amazing. If they ever have the Austrian soufle pancake on the menu it's a must order. Truly memorable dessert. The pastry counter is full of delectable choices and it's really hard to decide on what to get. I really enjoyed the roll cake, ham and cheese sandwich.  The canele is the only thing I wouldn't get again. On the lunch menu we really loved the Filipino fried rice so much so we ordered a second order. If you like coffee don't skip out on getting your favourite espresso drink. The mocha here is really great. During breakfast and lunch hours there are no reservations so do expect to wait in line on the weekends. The line moves pretty fast and it's open seating when you get into the restaurant.

This place used to be very good. Note* they have a 4% healthy fee (whatever that is).  Havent been here in a long time and missed their avocado toast. The wait was the usual, long lines outside that would take about 30 minutes before you can choose bakery goods and order. After you order, they give you a number and you find a random seat and food will come. The avocado toast for back then was very flavorful. It had a yuzu dressing, crunchy bits, and seasoning on top. Now you can barely taste the dressing and its bland. The adobo fried rice would have been good if the rice wasnt hard. It felt like i was biting into uncooked rice. The potato pancakes were good but not as crispy as it should be. The latte tasted mostly of milk with a hint of matcha. So the rose matcha latte tasted like a floraly milk. Their blueberry tart was good. It wasnt too tart and it was sweet. But for the price im not sure its worth it. A little sad that this place went downhill. I guess it got too popular? Street Parking is hard to find so you have to valet since there isnt a parking lot.

We've been to République many times for brunch, but never for dinner--so we finally tried it tonight while celebrating my son's birthday, and we had a great experience with the family. Dinner felt like a tasting-style, shared-plate experience, and everything we ordered was top notch. The bread and butter was a hit as always, the pastas were amazing, the steak was cooked perfectly, and the Dover sole, deboned tableside, was fresh and clean-tasting. Their execution is consistently impressive. The staff was very friendly, and the restaurant is beautiful at night with all the lights. The overall service felt polished--they changed our plates with each course and kept the meal moving at a nice pace. The one area for improvement was with the team clearing plates and resetting the table. They were very fast and efficient, but at times a bit abrupt, often reaching between us without warning. It caught my daughter off guard more than once when someone suddenly squeezed between her and my son. A simple "excuse me, may I take your plate?" and serving from the outside would make things feel smoother. Even slowing down just a tad when taking or placing plates would maintain that first-class experience rather than giving off a "we're so busy and rushing" feeling. We also found the dessert menu a bit underwhelming compared to their incredible bakery selection during the day--still good, just not as exceptional. Overall, it was a wonderful dinner and a great place to celebrate a special occasion. We'd definitely return to try more of their seasonal dishes.

I stopped by around 11:30 on a weekday for lunch with a party of 7. I was actually surprised we were able to find seats for everyone to sit together that easily. I went with the steak frites, medium rare. The steak was really tender, though it lacked a bit of flavor on its own, but the sauce definitely helped out. The fries were great, too. Honestly, for the price and the environment here, it's a really solid value. Some of our group also ordered the French toast, it is literally life-changing. You have to get it if you come here. I've been here before and I still think their breakfast options are a lot better than the lunch menu, but overall it was a good experience.

I've been always wanted to try this place because of the beautiful architecture and the food looks beautiful. I went here for brunch on a Wednesday and didn't have to wait very long. The food was full of flavor. I would recommend coming here.

We went around 11am and there was a line, but it didn't take long to order. When we walked in there was a ton of pastries that looked really good, but honestly they were a little stale. We also ordered an omelette and the shakshouka. Honestly I liked the cooked foods more as the omelette tasted great and it felt fresh. The shakshouka was a first for me and definitely not the last. The bread had a good char and was crunchy, it paired well with the rich and savory sauce and eggs.

LA style, this place has it! The vibes were immense, with an old fashioned decor and architecture that was built to impress. I loved the layout. The moment you enter, you were in the line to look at the counter display and order, which kept everything moving and efficient. Then you turn and are in the expansive seating area, which is packed and yet full of tables. The decor is darker, however well-lit. We had a spacious table with plenty of room to interact and eat. The potato pancake was decadent, with salmon and salmon roe galore. The avocado salad, pistachio and chocolate pastries and coffee were also amazing! We spent so much time just enjoying both the food and the ambiance and the staff were courteous and did not rush us at all! A great LA experience!

Came here for brunch on a weekend morning and the place had a line out the door. The wait wasn't too bad at least and we were in and seated post ordering after a few minutes. Space was a bit limited, but we didn't have to wait to find a table at least. Interior was really pretty and eclectic with the plants and decorations. Definitely felt really nice to just sit inside. Food came out fast enough - the quality was good, eggs were fresh and pastries were tasty. Some of them (pastries) weren't as good as they looked, but overall things were solid. Prices were a bit steep for the quantity, but otherwise the meal was good. Overall, I would not mind coming back for breakfast again to try more of their dishes. Thanks, Republique!

Soooo good! Absolutely loved everything I ordered. Brioche toast is a must try and it's so big it can definitely be shared. Grilled cheese was just what I needed after a long night. There was a line when we came on a sunday but it moved fairly quickly. You can come back to the register to add baked goods for takeaway if you're dining in. Once you're inside the ordering moves quickly so be prepared with your order. Parking wasn't too bad and we found street parking a block down.

Went here to use my Chase Sapphire dining credit. Foods pretty good, well known for their baguette and butter. Tried the hamachi crudo, crab roast, truffle risotto, and NY strip steak. Deducting a star because we ordered the steak medium but it came out rare. They took it back and fixed it but kinda surprised they missed the mark that bad with steak. They pre sliced it too so you can clearly see it was undercooked. Taking off a second star because they charge an optional 4% fee to help "pay for employee health insurance". It's auto included in the bill but you can ask it to be removed. It does not count as tip and does not go directly to employees. First time seeing this type of fee but felt a little slimy to just mention it in small fine print. But also shouldn't the employer be covering this, why should I be guilted into paying an extra 4% and then tip on top??? Food not good enough to have me come back.

Maybe I should have ordered something else but I just didn't think this was worth what I paid for. The brioche French toast was $21. It is a large piece of bread and it is light and fluffy and tastes good. But it's very sweet (even without maple syrup) and it's so airy, it's not filling. I ordered a side of bacon steak on the side to add some protein and the small piece of pork was $9.  It tasted ok, kind of chewy. For $30, I could have gone someplace else for a full breakfast that tastes just as good or better. I did buy a canelé and bomboloni to-go. Pastries were very good. Maybe just stick to buying their pastries or come for dinner.

Had dinner at République on a Tuesday night with friends and family and it reminded me again why this place is one of the best in LA. I've been a handful of times over the years and the consistency is just unreal. Chef Walter Manzke came by to check in and was incredibly warm and genuine, even taking the time to talk to my daughter and ask what she liked to eat. That kind of hospitality is rare. He ended up sending out a round of appetizers and champagne for the table, which made the night feel even more special. Just an all around wonderful person. The food was amazing from start to finish. Their bread and butter is still one of the most memorable things on the menu, simple but absolutely perfect. Every dish that came out was beautifully executed and full of flavor, and the cocktails were just as impressive, balanced, thoughtful, and worth ordering more than one. The space, the service, the energy, everything works together and never feels like it slips no matter how busy they are. It's one of those restaurants that delivers every single time. Overall 10/10 experience and easily one of my favorite places in the city.

So many pastries to choose! Definitely arrive early in the morning to have the best selection to choose from. My favorite was the coconut cake with yuzu curd and raspberry. We got there around 9am on a Sunday and were able to easily find free street parking (read the signs). There was a line and we waited maybe 10-20 minutes to order.  There is valet parking for $14. For breakfast, brunch, lunch: you order at the counter any pastries on display and at the register you order drinks and food from the menu. They give you a cup with a number on it and you find yourself a table carrying any pastries you purchased. They will bring your food/drink order out and that's the service. Note that they add a 4% service fee to the subtotal (you will get sales taxed on this added 4%). The prompted suggested tip options are (20-25%) so if you choose the suggested options, you are actually tipping over 24-29%. I did not like the added mental math to do while paying when there's a long line of people waiting behind you. The French toast was large and very soft from the brioche. It was delicious. They mushroom toast was great, but be aware that it is also very rich. Shakshuoka was great. I alternated bites of this dish to help balance out the richness of the mushroom toast. Croquet Madame was good too.

Had an audition nearby and a friend BEGGED me to bring her French toast. Since we both live in the valley we don't make it over here as much. Once my sister found out where I was headed she asked for a plate too. It's been years since I've been here and I recall now why it's always been on my list. The French toast is big, fluffy and definitely something that should be shared lol. Since I'm trying to be better about not having full meals of carbs and sugar that was the one thing I noted. I also cannot say I know what it tastes like because I was on an extended fast when I was their uber eats. One says it's the best French toast in LA, the other says it's pretty good but bland without the syrup. Normally I'd be the deciding factor but I'm choosing to detox like a crazy person right now - so you decide! Will def be back. Latest menu below. Street parking and valet avail. Inside is stunning with the natural light but it can get packed and LOUD so not ideal for a first date. And I did slide in at 1:50 to order though they close at 2 for lunch and they were beyond kind at placing my order.

This was my first visit to Republique for my best friend's birthday and it exceeded all expectations! From the ambiance, service, execution and cocktail/wine selection was 10/10. The highlight eats were our two starter amuse bouche bites: cheese ball and mini pate tart. Both came on a cute tea tier and we all said we would happily eat 100 of each! The crudos and salad was refreshing and presentation was stunning. The iconic bread and butter was also a win...I took an extra one home since it was so good. Our overall experience was fantastic and can't wait to come back to celebrate a loved one here

Been wanting to try this place for a while now, it is on so many "must try" places in LA so I had to go see what the hype is about.  We came on a Saturday morning at around 830 and there was no line, but the line quickly wrapped around the building after.  You order at the counter along with the baked goods and self-seat yourself.  It was a bit overwhelming for us to figure out what to order because it moved so fast so it would help to know the menu ahead of time: The food: -lobster omelette (good but wouldn't get again, nothing extraordinary) -kimchi fried rice (also good but wouldn't get again) -short rib burrito (delicious enchilada style burrito, would def get again) -mushroom toast (so good and would get again!$ -the PASTRIES (the saving grace of this place and why I'm rating it a 4/5 and not a 3/5) everything we got was so good and probably the only reason why I'd be back The pastries were the highlight for me and why I'll be back.  Is it the best brunch spot in LA? Not at all, but the it's a solid spot to try.

Food is great, food is average, service is sucks. Open seating, me and my kid had to keep getting utensils, condiments, napkins, water, to go box ourselves because they were so busy and even though we put 20% tip for $34. Two stalls bathrooms only. Overall it was ok. Ambiance would be very nice if it was not overly crowded.

For a morning deal we were 1st in line during the springtime cold l.a. morning, and de oded to be people free in the back outside tables semi covered and like French styled patisserie a d coffee [forgot what roaster] and rep.of tea, this was x3 visits a d actually phenomenal. Period You can see why with the lines and running out early. The menu changes but be sure a d see all of it prior to ordering. Seasonal coffee drinks as well. Saw the donut guyz showed up.[3] to.review, and knew this was gonna be great I have a Professor form L.A. Law School that goes here and appreciates some organic and free range item dishes on their menu Before we left back to SFO we had to get a gift. Ard a d some pastry for the reverse trip. Some of their highlights are breakfast too  crowded for Lunch for us high ceilings to some bar stool.seating. nothing Nothing on the menu we didn't enjoy 10's across. Will return everytime to West Hollywood. Comps to Le Chef the curaot the front mgmt and back of house for art of food! Don't miss when in L.A.
