Please click the link to fill out the corresponding information. We are looking forward to hearing from you. http://bit.ly/LousCrew Best, Michelle Martinez Lou Malnati's Pizzeria
Great place! Just be aware this location is take out only. Love the food but don't expect to dine-in. Go to other locations for that. They are very nice and make tasty pizza!

Wow for deep dish Chicago pizza! Talk about a heavy meal of delicious. Lou Malnati's is not the place you hear about to go when visiting Chicago to try Chicago-style pizza, but I'm sure glad we discovered it! Great selection, great beer, and great service! I would recommend trying this place if you're new to Chicago-style pizza, or if you're wanting to try a different place. We shared a house salad between three of us with a medium Malnati Classic. We finished it, and we were happily stuffed.
Thank you for your review, Jaime! We are happy to hear you enjoyed your deep dish pizza and had a great experience with our staff. We look forward to serving you again soon!
A true Chicago classic! It's even delicious with delivery!! The wings are on point too...definitely recommend!

Can't visit Chicago without a traditional deep dish pizza! I would have initially opted for Giordano's but was told that Lou Malnati's was the best in town. Now I know why they say so! We didn't dine in since we were challenged on time but their carry out service met my expectations. We placed an order over the phone and in 45 mins our pizza was ready. Talk about a pizza baked to perfection. I typically don't finish my entire slice but couldn't let the crust go to waste. Will certainly make this my casual places to visit every time I am in the area.

Steve DimaSteve Dima 2 reviews 27 minutes ago Had my brother pickup 3 frozen deep dish pizzas to bring back to Belleville, Il for me. Now, I've always liked Chicago style pizza over St. Louis style, but upon opening the pizzas I found them to be nothing like in the restaurant. The pizzas were only maybe half as thick as the crust was high.  And they were not very big pizzas for the price. I've seen a Pizza Hut pizza as thick as these. It did taste good but when I think of Chicago style, I envision thick pizza as in a "pie". Disappointed

Had my first experience with Chicago Pizza here and it was outstanding. The cheese bread was a great appetizer. Our server was upbeat and attentive which made for a great experience. If you're looking for really good Chicago Pizza I'd recommend Lou Malnati's!

So we're in Chicago and I'm like "I've gotta get me some authentic deep dish"! Where to go? Lou's of course! We had the house salad with the creamy lemon dressing, garlic bread, and the Lou's classic pie (sausage). The salad was really good and the garlic bread w/marinara was a nice hold over as it takes about 45 minutes to cook the pizzas. The pizza came and it was ok. I really wanted to be blown away, but I wasn't. The crust was really crispy around the edge and I think it needed more sauce on top. Service was spot on and the prices were good, but I guess we're just not fans of the deep dish.
The buttery crust is what makes this pizza great ! A must try if you want Chicago deep dish pizza!

This place was full of people and busy. One of the original pizza spots in Chicago. You may have to wait quite a bit for a table, but the good thing is that you can order your pizza prior to being seated. We ordered to Lou's pizza, we waited over 30mins to get seated and another 15plus mins to get our pre ordered pizza. To be honest i was expecting a WOW moment, but i was content with the pizza. I didnt like the flavorless crust, idk maybe its just a personal thing where i like flavor in my pizza crust, but this pizza was lacking flavor in the crust. I get it! Ok, its a deep dish pizza and thats the important part but again i wasn't impressed. I might give this place another try from another location to give it a second shot... but who knows.

This location supposedly opens at 11, but we called at 10:30 am and someone picked up and said they'd have our order ready by 11:15. Since we were on a time crunch we were pretty happy. This is a carry out & delivery location only, but you can eat at the park across the street or walk a block or two or down and eat at the picnic tables outside. No gimmicks, just fresh, lean sausage, delicious sauce, great cheese, and amazing Buttercrust. Perfectly baked. As I neared the end of my slice, I was seriously sad that it was about to end. The very best deep dish in Chicago.

I have to write this review relative to the pizza at Pequod's, as these are two of Chicago's favored deep dish pizza spots. My sole complaint about Pequod's was that their crust was too thick and also too yeasty. Lou Malnati's crust was thinner, crispier, and generally more flavorable. However, Pequod's toppings blew Lou Malnati's out of the water. I got the same toppings on both pizzas (pepperoni, mushrooms, and sausage), and Pequod's toppings tasted fresher and came in more abundance. The toppings at Lou Malnati's seemed to share real estate like a strip mall while the toppings at Pequod's were layered on top of each other more like an apartment complex. The Lou Malnati's sauce was better though, as it was more robust and had big chunks of solid tomato in every bite. Both are worth a stop if you're in Chicago, but my preference leans towards Pequod's due to the quality of their toppings.

Ate here because many people recommended it. Also, when you come to Chicago, deep dish is a must I feel? The wait here was 1 hour + but they had an efficient system that allowed you to see what number in line you were & they texted you when your table was ready. So I did like their service. The food overall was not over the top amazing but it was good! I have definitely had better pizza, so the deep dish did not stand out to me but like I said if you come to Chicago, this is something that you have to do for the experience. Good service & nice people! Next time I am in Chicago, I'll probably order and pick up :)

yes! Yes! YES! I finally got the opportunity to eat some authentic Chicago Deep Dish pizza. This location was a take out only, so I can skip a lot about the restaurant environment and get straight to the food. I am quite the pizza enthusiast, so I was curious about what actually made a Chicago deep-dish pizza so unique. Well, I purchased a Malnati Chicago Classic with "Lou's lean sausage, some extra cheese and vine-ripened tomato sauce on Buttercrust," After the first bite, my taste buds were quite confused with how amazing this pizza was. Cheese upon cheese upon cheese upon cheese. I had a slice that ends up being filling due to the amount of cheese it has. The crust sold me. To begin with, I am not a fan of crusts unless they are filled with cheese/pepperoni/gold. I am that guy that leaves crusts in the pizza box. However, this crust is like none other. It's crispy and flakey and garlic and butter and and and..you get the point. Also, if you are dying to try this pizza, they do ship to their pizza in the U.S. ;) http://www.tastesofchicago.com/category/Lou_Malnatis_Pizza

This review is for the neighborhood takeout Lou Malnati's near Wicker Park. The location is tucked into the back of a small strip mall, but still serves legit deep dish pies for takeout and frozen. There is a small amount of parking, but be careful during peak times. During the course of one night, I purchased both a frozen pie and had a fresh baked one delivered. Baking the pie in the oven was a new experience. I am used to take and bake pizzas in California, but I tried something new on my Chicago trip. If you follow the directions including oiling the pan, the results are pretty close to the original. Be warned that the frozen pies are small, so you may still have to order another one for delivery if your deep sausage butter crust desires are not met. Lou's is always awesome, and having a dedicated take out with frozen take and bake is a good option for everyone.

so glad we tried this place! we actually only waited about 15 mins to get seated at the bar on a wednesday night around 7pm. we came here for my boyfriends birthday and we were so happy we chose to celebrate here. the two people that helped us was antonio and issa and they made the experience 10x better. they were very attentive and friendly and just easy to talk to. gave us good recommendations and good vibes. we both really liked our drinks and were happy with the spread the food came out. we got to eat the bone marrow first which also came with this really good sauce it was almost like a meat jam but was so good on the bread and then put some of the bone marrow on for the perfect bite. now the burger, you just have to try it because it really is that good. the sauce in it was so good and it just had a really good flavor. it was just an elevated burger. we got fries as well and we shared the burger so it we were really full after. the server brought out ice cream with a candle and some sort of chocolate sauce too which just made the overall experience. we were really happy with the service and food and it just made my bfs bday that much more special and memorable.

Despite all the hype, it's really an average smash burger. This is a place that has capitalized on social media hype and people wanting to say they've been here and thus are cool and trendy. But it is seriously just a greasy smash burger. Their fries are good, and actually stand out more than the burger. Everything is overpriced. I don't know why people complain about the wait; do some research like a responsible adult. I never just walk into a place and expect to be immediately seated, I call first - like anyone who has some sense. If they tell you the wait is 2 hours and you have 2 hours to kill, there are a bunch of bars in the area where you can have some drinks and an appetizer (and not feel like you're stiffing Au Cheval; they're the ones with the 2 hour wait, what do they expect people to do?) Not much to say about the decor or ambience; it's a typically loud West Loop bar with mostly 20 - 30 somethings all trying to one-up each other with their trendiness that instead makes them all basically clones of each other. It is crowded, and you're a moron if you think any place like this is suitable for your 5 year old. That's not the restaurant's fault - it's not Chuck E Cheese. Often I wish Yelp offered a 1/2 star option, because there are places that are a 4.5 or a 3.5. Not in this case. 3 stars is spot-on.

I have tried a lot of burgers but nothing has topped Au Cheval. I can never quite finish one but every single bite is packed with flavor. It seriously hits every taste bud. Adding the pork belly and egg takes it to another level. The space is cozy and intimate but be prepared to wait. It can be anywhere from 30 minutes to a couple of hours. Your best bet is to put your name in and wait for the text alert. Thankfully Small Cheval spots are around when I need a quicker fix. As for parking it is a bit tight with valet street parking and nearby lots as your options.
Great experience, food and drinks

Went to Small Cheval and Au Cheval back to back on consecutive days. Both were fabulous. We went to Au Cheval when they opened on a Monday and only had a 15-minute wait. I don't know that I would wait 4-5 hours to eat here, yet it was delicious! We each ordered burgers, as well as shared fries and hash browns.  The hash browns were a bit too crispy for my tastes, but still good. Others in our party loved them. The burgers were cooked to perfection and the taste out of this world! As busy as they were, the food is served fast and the portions filling! Isa was a great server and made sure our drinks were always topped off.

We were heavily recommended this place by a friend and boy it was worth it. We showed up on a Sunday around noon, only had a 45min wait, which was not bad at all compared to our original attempt on Friday night! We were seated near where I could watch the line work, which I appreciated as someone in the food industry. Our server was extremely friendly and helpful, explaining the quirks of the menu as well as his own suggestions for us to try. The burgers themselves were amazing. Easily in my top 5 favorite restaurant style burgers of all time. The tender peppered bacon is the perfect touch for these burgers. If you can withstand the wait, it's truly a wonderful time at Au Cheval.

It's burger time! I was so excited to come experience the Au Cheval burger. I must tell you, I love burgers, but I love big juicy flavorful burgers. The patties here, are very thin. They put a double patty, with the delicious caramelized, bacon and egg. It makes up for the tiny little patties that you experience with your burger. The service is outstanding. I'm gonna tell you, quick and very efficient. I really wanted to like these thin, tiny patties, but I just couldn't. However... I always like me some skin on french fries.
Best.Burger.Period! You need to come here as soon as they open, no reservation.. you need to get in line/waitlist.

Au Cheval does not need anymore positive reviews and is a classic staple of Chicago, and one of my favorite burgers of all time. You will need to either come off hours for a shorter wait, or be prepared to wait for several hours. It's nice that you can be texted when your table is ready, because there are so many other restaurants and bars you can kill time at before coming back for your beloved burger. A warning that the standard burger already comes with two patties, so if you get an extra patty it is a total of 3. Definitely add the delicious thick cut peppered bacon to the burger (and I am not even usually a bacon person), and the egg if you want a bit of extra goo. We've also tried the fried chicken which was delicious, but if your mind is set on just burger, I'd recommend sticking to that. If you are with a small group that wants a bit of variety and is willing to share burgers, I'd recommend adding the chicken.

Enjoyed lunch here when we touched down in Chicago. The restaurant was quite busy, which is always a good sign. The inside of the restaurant is a bit compact, but super friendly. Great music  was playing the entire time, which had me rocking in my seat. Our server was super nice and helpful with the menu. We went for the single cheeseburger and the bologna sandwich. Both were good, but the burger waa wAaay better in my opinion.  A must try, and you only need a single.  We added bacon, with the egg, Soo good. I took off one star because I think the burger is a bit pricey, and the bologna wasn't all that. Otherwise this place was legit and I'd definitely return.

I am not by any means someone who goes out of their way for a burger, let alone craves one. I would equally be pressed to give an establishment 5 stars solely for a burger but this place defies all odds. Au Cheval was recommended to me during a work trip and I am SO glad I gave it a shot. Easily the best burger I've ever had, so much that I ordered it twice during my stay. Would highly recommend, their burgers are life changing.

Au Cheval was solid overall. The burger absolutely lived up to the hype, and the fries and root beer were great as well. I deducted a star because of the service. Our waitress forgot to put in our appetizer order, which is understandable and mistakes happen. After we finished our burgers, she brought us our check. We kindly reminded her that we were still waiting on our chicken to come out. She apologized and said she would bring us an order of chicken to go. She comped the chicken, which I appreciated. However, as tourists, we were looking forward to enjoying the full meal in the restaurant. Since there were several open tables at the time, it felt a little strange to be encouraged toward takeout instead of being able to stay and enjoy the appetizer there. Having to walk to the hotel with the chicken also noticeably affected the quality and overall experience. Overall, the food was great, but the service experience kept it from being a five-star visit.

One of my students, who was from Chicago, highly recommended Au Cheval to me. He actually recommended it for their cocktails being that it was one of the best places he's had a bourbon drink. After doing my own research I found that it was recognized as having one of the best burgers in America. For that alone I had to try the place. Au Cheval was my first stop after flying into Midway. I knew that the place didn't take reservations, so I gambled with the fact that I was dropping by on a Monday night. No way that the place would be busy. Boy, was I wrong. I arrived around 7:30pm and the place was packed. I put myself on the waitlist and thankfully they add you to an automated system where you get texted when your seat is almost ready. I went to the bar next door thinking I was going to be there for a while, but I really only waited for 15-20 minutes. When I checked in, one of the front desk hostesses kindly offered to hold my luggage for me.  They must get that a lot, because they have a whole ticketed coat check system. I had a seat at the bar where service was great and vibes were everything. I was feeling the old school hip hop instrumentals while waiting shortly for my food and drink. My server was friendly and helped to offer modifications that worked to my dietary preferences. I don't eat pork, which I understood was a very popular add-on to the burger, so he suggested I try it with foie gras as the next best thing. I got a single cheeseburger (comes with 2 patties) and added a sunny side egg and foie gras. I thought the burger was delicious. It was so flavorful and well seasoned, and the egg and foie gras gave the burger extra richness. The burger sans add-ons was $30, so it came out to ~$44 with everything. Was it really worth that price? Debatable. That said, I would still recommend this place and want to try their chilaquiles!

Stopped by Au Cheval in Chicago this past weekend for my birthday trip with my girls and it was honestly one of the best burgers I've had. The Single Cheeseburger comes with 2 patties with the addition of their bacon and egg. Highly recommend this spot for a quick bite! It is a small bar spot with tight seating but it really wasn't a bother.

Best burger in the city (so far) - definitely recommend adding the eggs + bacon, which was the highlight of the meal. Meat was cooked perfectly. We just walked around West Loop while waiting for ~1.5 hours on a Saturday afternoon, so the time went by pretty quickly. Definitely worth the wait!

While still a four-star burger for me, subtle changes have made it not quite the best anymore. The patties are smaller and the bun is different now. I was even there the day the bun changed and the cooks and manager were impressed I noticed--it's like McDonald's changing the Big Mac sesame seed bun! There's some things you just don't do. The bologna sandwich is very salty and garlicky, not quite as balanced as the original. On the plus side, service is still pretty good, and the fries are excellent, along with the well-made cocktails and tasty chicken. While three-hour waits will ensure a disappointing meal, I've noticed the wait has been more reasonable as the hype has died down. 3.75 stars overall

Anytime a restaurant or dish achieves the distinction of being the best in the city, country or world several things will usually happen. .. One, crowds and wait times will grow exponentially. Two, service will suffer until the business adapts to new found fame. Three, sheep will rave and blindly profess their love and adoration (while affirming it's the best in the entire city despite never traveling South of Roosevelt). It may be the best, but how would you know? Lol Four, Foodies with well versed palates will mostly agree with the awesomeness bestowed, but some will reasonably disagree. Five, haters who know very little about the nuisances of delicious food and the science behind it will overdo it with unreasonable critiques. Six, every new competitor will be touted as the "fill-in-the blank Killer". Au Cheval has experienced each of these. Being ranked a top burger has been controversial to some, but that's one of the great things about food. We're all entitled to like or dislike whatever we choose. But. ..with that being said anyone who says this isn't a great burger is just plain wrong ;-)

As everyone else has yelped the burgers are simple and once you add the thick cut bacon, a perfect balance of smoky, salty, rich and cheesy awesomeness.  Aside from the burgers, fries and drinks I can't say I particularly like or dislike anything else on the menu, but what else do you need, lol.  The Vieux Bonal is greatness in a glass. Try it.
Best fries and burger I've ever had. Add the egg and bacon as well- it's worth it. Expensive but worth it.

That burger at Au Cheval is genuinely life-changing. You have to add both the bacon and the egg -- the egg is what makes it true "au cheval" style in classic French culinary tradition. The bun is impossibly buttery, the bacon is thick-cut and smoky, and the egg is cooked perfectly so it melts into every bite. It's served with an aggressively salty pickle that cuts through the richness in the best way possible. And don't skip the bone marrow -- it comes with thick slices of toast and a berry jam that completely makes the dish. The sweetness against the rich, savory marrow is unreal. The vibe is effortlessly cool -- low lighting, great music, and laid-back servers that make the whole experience feel relaxed and unpretentious. Tip: Make sure you put your name down a couple hours before you actually want to eat. Stop by lone wolf bar right next door for a cocktail before

This nonstop talked about burger was good but was it the greatest burger in all of Chicago and America? No. Definitely solid though just left me feeling confused as to why people are in love with it. I think it's one of those things you have to try and see for yourself. They don't take reservations so make sure you prepare and get there early to put your name in!

Finally made it to Au Cheval and it lived up to the hype. The staff was great, and Natalia especially stood out--very polite and patient with everyone waiting to get on the waitlist, which made the whole process feel smooth even during a busy time. Started with their root beer on tap and it was excellent. My friend and I split a single cheeseburger and a double cheeseburger with egg so we could try both. After tasting both, I'd probably go with a single cheeseburger and add egg and their bacon next time--that combo seems like the sweet spot. The ambiance was great--definitely crowded, but still enough room to wiggle around and move without feeling packed in. Bathrooms were gender neutral, which was nice and convenient. Parking was easy with street parking nearby, and since I went on a Monday Randolph wasn't too hectic. Overall a solid burger spot, and I can definitely see why it consistently lands in the top 5 burger spots in the city. Now I'm curious how different Small Cheval is compared to the original.

The vibes were amazing. Dim lighting, great loud music, and a fun energy without feeling chaotic. Solid 8/10 atmosphere. Service felt a little off at first, probably because our original server was about to leave, but once we switched, everything was fine. 6/10. Now the burger... it might actually be one of the best I've had. It tasted familiar, like something you could make at home, but somehow still fantastic and delicious. Adding the bacon and egg made it perfect. Everything went so well together. 9.5/10. Yes, it's around $29 which is kinda wild, but it really is that good. The roasted marrow bones were incredible. The sweet onion jam with the toast was such a good combo. 9.5/10. The cocktail was plain and felt like it was missing something but it was still delicious. 8/10. The cheeseburger is definitely worth the hype and get the bone marrow too!

This venue is perfect for both elegant breakfasts and memorable parties. Breakfast is beautifully presented, fresh, and flavorful, creating a refined start to the day. For gatherings, the space is stylish and welcoming, with attention to detail that makes every event feel special. The staff is attentive and professional, ensuring that both meals and celebrations go smoothly. A wonderful choice for anyone looking to combine great food with a sophisticated atmosphere.

Heard a bunch of great things about this place. Ended up waiting a bit longer than anticipated, but it was all good. The drinks were decent but not fantastic. The burger was tasty. I would go back but probably not wait over an hour to be seated.

Au Cheval has a reputation for its delicious burgers and long lines. Luckily enough, I came right when they opened for lunch and was able to get a table immediately. Fun fact about the burgers here--a single burger has two patties, a double has three, and so on. I came hungry, so I was pleasantly surprised that my single cheeseburger has two patties in it. The burger itself was very enjoyable BUT I wouldn't say that it was mind blowing my any means. I added an egg which enhanced it, but dare I say, this burger wasn't even close to one of the best I've had. Coming from California, my husband made a comment saying that while it's good, In n Out is better (which although In N Out makes an amazing burger, it's fast food so we didn't think the two would be comparable). So while we enjoyed our meal, we were underwhelmed by the food. On the positive side, service here is extremely friendly! The vibes here are cool too because it's like a lux diner. So would I recommend this spot? Maybe if there's no line. But absolutely not if I had to wait more than 10 minutes.

The staff here are so friendly. They were always laughing and smiling. They answered all our questions and was able to make recommendations based on our answers. We decided to try the famous bone marrow, a double cheese burger and classic fries. Surprisingly, a single burger is actually a double patty burger. And a triple patty is actually a triple patty. The ambiance was a relaxed chilled bar vibe. They had bar seating and booth seating.

10/10 recommend! From the moment you walk in, the customer service is on point. The staff is super attentive and really knowledgeable about the most popular items. They even offered me an off-menu burger with a single patty (instead of the standard double), which I appreciated. I also loved the classic, vintage vibe of the restaurant. We sat at the bar and got to watch the chef work thanks to the open kitchen concept. And let's talk about it: the burgers and fries were amazing, and the cocktails were absolutely top-tier. If you're in the Chicago area, you have to check them out!

Au Cheval is one of those iconic burgers that define a city. I think this particular burger definitely needs to be topped off with a egg over easy to give all its glory with the juice and messiness. Is it a lot of money for a burger? Yes. But these are the days with a $20 burger and at least you are guaranteed a solid burger and flavors rather than something that is dry or lackluster.

Root beer on draft and sitting at the bar watching all the cooking magic happen! The kale caesar salad is always good and my go to burger is the classic single cheeseburger. My husband loves to add bacon to his burger too. Service is always friendly, and we were seated right away when we walked in. Ambience is casual and cool inside.

The man I have a crush on at work highly recommended Au Cheval!  He said this is the best burger he ever had!  And he was not lying!  Here is what you need to know: -No reservations accepted -They are busy all the time so expect to wait; sometimes hours (but it is sooo worth it) -When you arrive make sure to check in at the host stand and they will text you when your table is ready -There are other bars within a block that you can grab a drink or walk around -They will not seat you until your entire party has arrived -No you can't just sit at the bar area -All the wait staff were very friendly and provided great recommendations Let's get to the good part...food and drinks! -Get the burger and yea you can add tomato, lettuce, jalapeños, etc -If you're kinda bougie you can add foie gras on the side -For my bacon eaters, YES!  We wanted to try on the side, and it's tasty, fatty, thick, and seasoned -One order of fries can be shared w/ 3 people (they  weren't my fav item and to be honest you'll need the tummy room for the burger) -Lemonade is made fresh, was slightly tart but they offer simple syrup on the side to sweeten it up, loved -I took a sip of the Bloody Mary (never tried before) and it was so seasoned it almost tasted like a cold tomato soup (chef's kiss) This is 2 thumbs up, 5 stars, and very satisfied!  Do not think about it and GO!

Au Cheval is exactly who they think they are !!!! Yessssss! I've been wanting to go here for several years but not a fan of waiting for hours. I went very late after a play and was able to get a seat for one at the bar! It was still crowded at 10pm. The burger was juicy and flavorful. Service was quick and kind. I will be back !

This place is so good, I brought my fiancé here during our layover in Chicago. I've been fortunate enough to visit Au Cheval twice now, and it seems I've tried most of the menu. My first visit was with some people who didn't particularly *need* to try more than just the burger here, so that left a lot for me to try in the future. And because my fiancé and I have no self control when it comes to wanting to try all the good food, we ordered way too much food for two people on this last visit (and now there's basically nothing left for us to try). As expected, we were quoted a possible hour and forty-five minute wait to be seated (around 2pm on a Saturday). They took my name and phone number, and we went off to get drinks next door. The text they send has a link you can follow to check your place in line, so I did that after we finished our first drinks. We were still in the 60+ minute section, so we closed out and walked to a different bar for another drink and an appetizer. The appetizer was a mistake for many reasons: 1. We ended up ordering way too much food at Au Cheval, even without having first eaten the appetizer 2. All the food at Au Cheval was exponentially more tasty and I wish I would have had more stomach space for the good food 3. We hadn't even received our appetizer when we got the text notifying us that our table was ready at Au Cheval So I guess I wrote all that to provide some tips: the portions are very fair and you probably can't eat as much as you think here; don't order food elsewhere while you wait to be seated here; the wait time they give you could change dramatically if a bunch of people waiting in line before you exit the queue. You should also know that this restaurant is kinda small. You may be seated at the bar if that's all that's available. People wait for an hour and then get seated at the bar sometimes...it happens. The best way to describe the atmosphere in this establishment is like "moody diner"? Kinda sultry...kinda salty. The service was awesome and welcoming, and even though a couple items came out incorrect, everything was delicious and we don't regret anything. It would take me a lot to be constantly busy all day every day and still make every customer feel special, but somehow, our guy did it. Although we did order too much food (for even our small table to hold), we still thought about it all lovingly as we were horribly bloated later on. Anyway, the burger was just as good as I remembered, and my fiancé was so pleased with it. We don't often go out to try burgers from new places, but we can definitely tell a good burger from a bad one. I think the matzo ball soup was my favorite item besides the burger, and if I ever manage to come back here in the cold, I will definitely be getting that again. The ball and the broth were both so light and flavorful, and the soup sits differently in your stomach when you're also filled with a bunch of meat and bread. There's somehow more room for the soup. Best wishes to them, and to everyone interested in trying this place out. It's worth the wait. You're worth the wait.

Au Cheval absolutely lives up to the hype. The space has that dark, vintage diner feel that's both cozy and full of energy from the moment you walk in. The burger is the star for a reason--insanely juicy, rich, and perfectly balanced with melty cheese, and their signature sauce. Adding bacon and an egg takes makes it extra. The fries are crispy and tasty, especially with the delicious garlic aioli. Sitting at the bar gives you the perfect view to observe how all the deliciousness happens. Service is friendly and efficient even when it's packed. Yes, there's usually a wait, but it's completely worth it for a burger this memorable.

I'm on a mission.. We weren't able to make it to Au Cheval during the last Chicago visit. So, this time was a must. The burger game in NYC and Chicago has upped x10 over the last few years. Au Cheval was once listed as the top burgers in the US by many food publications. Since then and the intro to American Wagyu to the burger scene, a few other top the list. After a disappointed wait at Bavette's to try their burger, a walk in visit to Au Cheval was on the itinerary. 10:45 am on a Sunday was the entry point. They open at 11 am and there were already people inside seated and ready to order. I've heard people wait 2-3 hours to get in. So, getting in early is the secret sauce. A spot on the diner counter is a must watching the action of the burger flipping and grease flying. The inside of Au Cheval is dim lighting, dark wood, leather button seating gives off a  warm feeling. The onflow of conversations and upbeat mood makes this place a happy place. The burger here is a must. Supposedly the fried bologna sandwich is too. A single cheeseburger here is actually a double burger and a double burger is actually a triple. They tell you upfront in case you have heart problems. I guess that's their disclaimer. Adding thick cut pepper bacon is must and you'd be disappointed if you didn't coming from out of town. I didn't want a meat ache so a single it is with thick cut pepper bacon. This burger on 3 layers had juices oozing out. The slice of pickle made me feel good of at least having a veggie on the side.  Some prefer to add a fried egg and a side of fries. That's just cholesterol overload and plaque buildup. The rest of the menu here look great and on our next visit I'll have to try other items, crispy potato hash, chiliquiles, foie gras. Overall, a good burger but not sure if I'd wait more than 30 minutes for it. I have my preferences and I'd prefer the Peter Luger burger over this and a few other places in LA.  Great experience, good service and good vibes.

Ok, I finally made it here and it exceeded all expectations. How could I possibly love a burger that I have to queue for 45+ minutes? Well, I did. Firstly, get the bone marrow (1/2 order if its just 2 of you). Delicious, especially paired with the jam on toast. Save a little for your burger! Fries, fresh. Not even requiring dipping sauce, though the aioli is quite good. Burger. Yes, yes, and yes. Loved the little pickle slices on it. So tasty, perfect balance of savory, umani, cooked to perfect temperature. Two of us shared the half order of marrow, 1 side of fries, and 1 double burger; it was more than enough. We took an order of chicken wings home with us too (savory, sweet, sticky, fall off the bone).

Excellent. Burger amazing. Goey, tender meat melts on your mouth, dressed to perfection. Fries and aioli-excellent. Bologna sandwich is on a whole level and league on her own. Porky, tender, cheesy, with the softest toasty butter bread. It's still hard to get a seat after all these years but if you can score it in the afternoon on a weekday, you hit the jack pot.

A must try burger spot in Chicago. Be prepared for a wait (usually 30min-1hour) but I promise it's worth the wait. The burgers are juicy, tender, and delicious. Don't forget to top it off with a sunny egg!

Glad I got to try the amazing 'Au Cheval' while in Chicago. We arrived around 11:30am last Saturday and put our names down. Luckily, we only waited 45 minutes, as I previously heard the wait can go for hours. Our group sat in a booth and ordered a couple of things to share. We started with a few drinks. The root beer on tap was quite sweet, but well enjoyed. I really liked the Arnold Palmer, which I learned that day was iced tea and lemonade. When the cheeseburger arrived, we instantly regretted not ordering the bacon on top. We waved another server down and asked for a side of bacon. When he returned, he kindly set it on the table and said, "On the house." What a wonderful surprise! It was also the most delicious thick-cut bacon I have ever had, and combined with this amazing, juicy burger, I felt I had gone to heaven and back. We ordered one burger and shared it amongst 4 people, and it was perfectly fulfilling. The fried chicken was a bit too salty for me, but the sweet and spicy flavour was great. I liked that they include thighs and wings. Finally, the blueberry muffin is a seared muffin with butter, chocolate, and jam on the side. The outside of the muffin is crusted in sugar, and I found that a bit too sweet, but the inside paired well with the toppings, and I'm glad I ordered it as the sweet dish of our brunch. One of our friends is a vegan (bless her for letting us drag her here) and opted for a nice alcoholic drink. The same gentleman who brought us the bacon walked by and served her a heaping plate of pickles on the house and said, "Everyone eats." This was the sweetest gesture ever! The pickles also paired really well with the rest of the food. Overall, I think the food was a bit heavy for me, but the amazing service and staff definitely made up for it. I will have to return one day to try some of the other menu items!

Au Cheval has long wait times and you can't place a reservation. In the end it is totally worth it to try one of their burgers. A fairly small spot but enough room to move around. Their burgers are done of the best burgers I have ever had. These burgers are massive and you can add bacon or an egg for an extra price. These burgers burger is topped with fried onions, Dijon mustard, pickles, and American cheese. Another standout was the bone marrow a great appetizer to start your meal. Fried are separate and those are delicious as well. Staff and service was great and now I know why this is one of the best burger spots in Chicago.

Beef patties were a nice medium / medium rare A lot of sameness in flavour (too salty and I was craving the pepper kick) I think I'd wanna do just the egg, pickles, no mayo next time ... creaminess from both the mayo and egg yolk was a little too much

After all these years, I still consider their bacon cheeseburger with an egg on top my favorite burger from anywhere in the country. The fries are great and staff is friendly.  Yes, you will have to wait for 30 minutes or so, but it is worth the wait!  Yum!

Great to see that a few years later (visiting for work), this place is still fantastic. One of, if not the, very best burger I've ever had. The added bacon and fried egg are worth the high price. Their fries are also some of the best I've had. Service was great also.

I've never spent so much money on a burger and at the same time decided it was worth it! The burger itself, given the quality, isn't so much at $15, but adding the egg ($3, worth it) and bacon ($7, worth it) bring the price up quite a bit. But it's a big burger and so very, very good. I should mention that the "single" is two burger patties and the "double" is three. I also got the fries, which were excellent, but it was so much food. Better to split an order of fries with someone. I wish I could be back in Chicago again sometime soon so I could eat here again.
